title: Figure 1.1  Evidence-to-defence architecture
alt_text: Nine-stage evidence-to-defence workflow. An inquiry route enters the Project Start Pack, then passes through the Problem, Evidence, Design, Execution, Claim, Argument, Editorial and Defence Readiness gates. TRACE operates transversally, and a failed condition reopens the responsible earlier gate.

title: Figure 1.2  Advice, authority and authorship map
alt_text: The student is central and remains responsible for authorship, verification, disclosure and defence. Supervisor advice, institutional authority, external organisational access and AI candidate assistance support the student without transferring responsibility.

title: Figure 2.1  Topic decision path
alt_text: Topic selection pathway from interest to a bounded problem, SCOPE, a route-specific question and feasibility evidence. A decision then leads to Continue, Narrow, Pivot or Stop, with only Continue and a scope-updated Narrow outcome progressing to the Problem Gate.

title: Figure 2.2  SCOPE framing canvas
alt_text: SCOPE framing canvas with five components: Scope, Constraints, Output, Proof and Exclusions. These converge on a tractable project, supported by an evidence basis and accompanied by explicitly unresolved uncertainty.

title: Figure 3.1  Evidence identity chain
alt_text: Evidence identity chain from search route and discovery record to a verified source object and a publication-to-study identity map. An unresolved identity is repaired before use; a resolved source is read, appraised and connected to a project decision and claim-linked evidence.

title: Figure 3.2  CORPUS records cycle
alt_text: CORPUS records cycle: Collect, Organise, Read, Probe, Use and Synthesise. Each activity produces a named record, and synthesis produces the Evidence Base Pack. The cycle returns to Collect only when evidence gaps remain.

title: Figure 4.1  Reversible driver-to-test chain
alt_text: Reversible driver-to-test chain. Evidence and authority define a driver and boundary, alternatives and criteria lead to a decision and trigger, a protocol artefact is early-tested, and the result either reopens an upstream decision, qualifies the boundary or retains the current version.

title: Figure 4.2  DECIDE conditional commitment cycle
alt_text: Six-step DECIDE cycle around a conditional commitment: Define, Establish, Construct, Inspect, Decide and Test. Early-test results retain, qualify or reopen the current commitment.

title: Figure 5.1  Candidate-to-admission chain
alt_text: Candidate-to-admission chain. An approved commitment becomes a bounded work unit with a frozen start state and candidate output. Primary artefact inspection leads to repair or repeat, local acceptance into the execution dossier or rejection and quarantine. Local admission is not thesis proof.

title: Figure 5.2  Bounded execution loop
alt_text: Bounded execution loop: Authorise and bound, Freeze state, pass a Safety Gate, Produce a candidate, Inspect and dispose, then Record and recover. Unsafe work stops for authority, and failed or rejected work remains in the record.

title: Figure 6.1  Evidence-to-claim ladder
alt_text: Nine-level evidence-to-claim ladder: Accepted work, Observe, Metric, Compare, Evidence, Interpret, Claim boundary, Bounded claim and Contribution. The figure prohibits output-to-claim and metric-to-contribution shortcuts.

title: Figure 6.2  Claim stress test and gate returns
alt_text: Claim stress test with six operations: Bound the claim, Match the route, Characterise uncertainty, Challenge counter-evidence, Reproduce or audit, and Decide the claim with a fallback. Outcomes are retain or qualify, repair or return, and reopen or suspend.

title: Figure 7.1  Gate records to thesis argument
alt_text: Gate records provide authorised inputs to an answer spine comprising question, route or method, evidence or result, boundary and contribution. A shared reuse bus connects spine elements to Introduction, Knowledge, Method, Results and Discussion, showing that records are sources rather than chapters.

title: Figure 7.2  Section and paragraph contracts
alt_text: Two writing controls. The section contract moves through Promise, Evidence, Reasoning, Boundary and Hand-off. The paragraph reasoning test moves through Claim, Evidence, Reasoning and Boundary, with a deletion test for material that changes nothing essential.

title: Figure 8.1  Semantic revision and proof control
alt_text: Two separate closure lanes. Semantic closure checks Study, Macro, Meso and Micro revision for identity preservation, returning to the responsible gate if not the same. Technical proof checks DOCX, story ranges, PDF and pages, repairing and repeating if the render is not clean.

title: Figure 8.2  One-study consistency lock
alt_text: One authoritative study controls three derivative layers: headline, manuscript and package. An equivalence decision either locks the derivatives or repairs the earliest divergent layer. Compression may shorten detail but may not alter study identity or claim scope.

title: Figure 9.1  Closure to defence readiness
alt_text: Defence-readiness chain from Closure through current Authority, Record and Performance set to a pass decision. Readiness checks cover Rules, Files, Disclosure, Evidence and Recovery, while one bounded contribution must remain stable.

title: Figure 9.2  One contribution across interfaces
alt_text: One bounded contribution is represented across four non-substitutable interfaces: the institutional record records it, the private evidence package preserves it, the demonstration and slides demonstrate it, and oral answers defend it. No interface can repair a contradiction in another.
